variants.name: Gull (Scrapyard Rescue)
variants.description: While the Starling was the first successful ship to use technology derived from alien ruins, the Gull is the most recent. The current increase in Korath activities has caused foraging for resources to become a risky endeavor, forcing the Remnant to develop a specialized freighter for hauling cargo from remote sites without revealing their presence to hostile aliens. 	The Gull has quickly proven its worth, allowing the Starling fleets to return to riskier activities while the Gull takes over the hazardous convoy routes. It is now the primary element of the Remnant's extra-territorial resource operations. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Gull's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Starling (Scrapyard Rescue)
variants.description: One of the strangest and most useful things that the Remnant have discovered in the abandoned worlds of the Ember Waste is alien cloaking technology. They have designed their scout ships to cloak when needed in order to explore alien territory without being seen... or to escape in a hurry after stealing something particularly valuable from those aliens. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Starling's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Peregrine (Scrapyard Derelict)
variants.description: The Peregrine is the first capital warship designed by Taely using fresh insights garnered from recent experimentation as well as renewed studies of the void sprites. Encompassing over a century of development since the last generation of warships was built, it is the forerunner of a new breed of Remnant ships. 	The Peregrine was designed along the lines of old-earth's fast-attack cruisers. Drawing on inspiration from its namesake, famed for being the fastest self-propelled lifeform on Earth, it is designed to strike hard and fast. It closes quickly with enemies to unleash devastating barrages in the opening seconds of combat. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Peregrine's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Quarg Wardragon (Blue Wardragon)
variants.description: The Wardragon is used by the Quarg as a light warship. It is an older design within the Quarg's fleets, supposedly less intimidating compared to their larger warships and thus more suitable for dealings with particularly nascent species.

variants.name: Leviathan (Hai Limit Breaker)
variants.description: The Betelgeuse Shipyards Leviathan has been in service since long before the Republic existed. Although considered today to be an outdated and clunky model, it is still a force to be reckoned with.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Scar's Legion → -0.1

variants.name: Mule (Hai Limit Breaker)
variants.description: The Mule is as much of a hodgepodge as its looks suggest. The Lionheart ship designers combined a good deal of cargo space with a decent amount of weaponry and even a fighter bay, and ended up with a ship that is mostly used as a freighter but can also be used as a warship because of its heavy armament and shields. This hodgepodge nature has its downside, though, namely its high crew requirement and the fact that any dedicated ship of the same cost will do better in a specialized role than the Mule will.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Scar's Legion → -0.1

variants.name: Firebird (Hai Limit Breaker)
variants.description: The Betelgeuse Shipyards Firebird is a warship with a long and storied past; Firebirds fought on both sides of the Alpha Wars over half a millennium ago, and although the equipment and systems have been upgraded continuously since then, the basic design remains almost the same. The Firebird is also a very rugged ship and easy to repair; supposedly a few of the Firebirds that fought in those wars are still in service today.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Scar's Legion → -0.1

variants.name: Corvette (Hai Limit Breaker)
variants.description: Incorporating new, experimental lightweight materials, the Lionheart Corvette combines the speed and agility of a fighter with the armament of a heavy warship. Its weak hull is more than compensated for by its advanced shielding matrix.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Scar's Legion → -0.1

variants.name: Headhunter (Hai Limit Breaker)
variants.description: The Headhunter is one of the newest ships designed by Lionheart: a versatile ship that can serve equally well for carrying cargo or for bounty hunting. As with many of Lionheart's designs, the hull is mostly composite fiber rather than metal, sacrificing armor strength for the sake of lighter weight and faster movement.
governmentEvents: Event "mgf: ngk resist pug invasion": MGF: NGK Hauling attitude toward Scar's Legion → -0.1

variants.name: Kasichara A'awoj (Jump)
variants.description: Originally designed as a luxury habitat for those wealthy enough to escape living on the polluted surface of Korath worlds, when the Korath were exiled, it was into these gargantuan "world-ships" they first crammed themselves into and fled to the core on. Nostalgically, the class was then renamed after the devastated and now forbidden Korath homeworld in honor of the Korsmanathi, ancestors of all Korath. 	Since the introduction of purpose-built city ships, these ancient vessels have mostly been decommissioned, turned into stations, or reconfigured into smaller, specialized vessels. Yet a few still ply the starlanes, crewed by those too restless to live on stations yet not bold enough to go on raids.

description.text: Unexplained power failures at Titania Station have reignited rumors that someone died during the station's construction. description.text: These ruined derelicts appear to be part of a Kor Sestor expeditionary fleet. With no jump drives, it must have taken this fleet centuries to arrive here. The largest ship is loaded with construction equipment. If these ships had managed to find a suitable planet to set up a base of operations, it could have lead to the return of the Kor Sestor. It is unknown how many more of these fleets are out there.

children.key: After going to the address where someone might be interested in buying your Blight Shadow eggs, you find yourself at what is likely an illegal zoo for exotic creatures.
A man in rugged attire approaches you. "G'day mate. What can I do yer for?"
"Let's see what you've got here..." The man looks over the eggs. "Weird ones, eh? I'll give ya 150000 for the lot of 'em."
"I was hoping for a better deal."
You take the money and leave the eggs at the zoo.
"Hmm..." The man looks over the eggs. "Tell ya what. How about I do the work of raising them and you get to keep one once it's fully grown?"
(This sounds like a bad idea. Better ask for money.)
"Alright. It's a deal." You both shake hands. He introduces himself as Gemini Jack. "Check back with me in a few months. Hopefully these things will have hatched by then."

values: An exotic animal zoo keeper on Greenrock who has agreed to raise some Blight Shadow eggs for me.
I've left the Blight Shadow eggs with Gemini Jack. I'm sure nothing will go wrong.

children.key: It's been a while since you left the eggs with Gemini Jack. When you check up on him and the eggs, he invites you to visit the zoo and see for yourself how they've grown.

He has some Blight Shadows locked up in a gigantic titanium holding tank. Anyone approaching the holding area carries a titanium shield large enough to hide behind. The shields look like they've taken quite a bit of abuse... "They're a dangerous lot, 'specially due to their intelligence. We have to keep repairing the tank because they can eat through the metal plating. Lead, iron, titanium... The type of metal doesn't matter if they're left alone long enough." He has them perform some tricks to demonstrate that they've been trained. "Go ahead and pick one."

It takes all day, but you manage to determine which of the creatures is best suited for you. The zoo workers load it into your cargo bay. The plan is to release it once you're in orbit. This entire scheme sounds ridiculous, but it's too late to back out now.

values: I have a pet Blight Shadow. What could go wrong?
It was a crazy idea to try keeping one as a pet. But the Blight Shadow that you hatched from an egg served you well in the time you had together.
Gemini Jack's exotic animal zoo was wiped out. I won't be able to get a new Blight Shadow to replace the one I lost from them.

children.key: You wonder how Gemini Jack is doing with the rest of the Blight Shadows. Maybe he could sell you a new one to replace the one you lost.

The titanium holding tank that the Blight Shadows were kept in is a blasted wreck. Something terrible took place here, but there's no one around to tell you what happened.

You hear a loud crunching sound coming from your cargo hold. When you check the security cameras, you see that the Blight Shadow eggs have hatched! The newborn Blight Shadows are tearing open the cargo hatch...

children.key: You receive an invitation from Prefect Chilia to meet at a Remnant weapons lab.
"Some of the egg samples you delivered were made available to us," he sings. "After several experiments, we managed to create this."
He presents you with a bulky long gun. "A prototype blight rifle. I would like for you to field test it for us."
"I'd be glad to field test it for you."
He hands the rifle to you. "May the Embers burn bright for you, Captain."

"It is a vicious weapon. It works by draining the energy from any creature it is used on. Such creatures are reduced to withered husks. One benefit of all this is that it charges itself whenever it drains a creature's life force." He sings all this in a light tone. Briefly, you wonder who or what was used for target practice in the earlier experiments. Perhaps it would be better to not think too much about that.
"We went through three eggs, and this is the result," he sings. "Hopefully we can acquire more eggs to continue our research."

values: I'll be testing a prototype Blight Rifle for the Remnant. This experimental weapon was developed as a result of their research on the Blight Shadow eggs I brought them.

children.key: It's been a while since you delivered Blight Shadow eggs to Plume. Do want to see what he's learned?

You find Plume alone, hunched over an operating platform. A Blight Shadow lies sedated on it, its body sliced open for dissection. Judging from its relatively small size, this is probably a hatchling. As you step into the room Plume looks up in surprise. "Ah, <first>! You startled me," Plume chants quickly. "These creatures are incredibly dangerous! The first ones to hatch immediately attacked." He sets down his tools and starts cleaning his hands.
"No, but the creatures escaped before we could study them." His notes trail off on a mournful tone. "We've put more vigorous safety protocols into practice with the remaining test subjects.

"The creature absorbs energy. Both light and heat are absorbed through its skin, imbuing it with the ability to cloak itself. It can also absorb fuel, energy, and heat from ships through a beam emitted by a special organ hidden amongst its tentacles. As I said, it is very dangerous. However it does seem to have a weakness." He takes a breath then continues, "While hunting down the escaped specimens, an ion storm swept through the system. Apparently, the ionic energy was somewhat disruptive to whatever internal organs regulate movement and cloaking."
That information could be useful. You thank Plume for his research and head out.

values: Plume's research on the Blight Shadows revealed that the ion storms native to the Ember Wastes are disruptive to some of their internal organs.
Plume mentioned that some of the Blight Shadows escaped. He never indicated if they were all caught...
These Blight Shadows are weaker than the ones you've encountered in Sestor space. They could just be hatchlings. Or maybe the Ember Waste is somehow inhospitable to them.

children.key: You find Plume pacing at the spaceport. "Captain <last>! A research team aboard the <npc> ventured out into Korath space to research the Blight Shadows and didn't return on schedule. We fear the worst has happened to them. Would you be willing to search for them?" The tone of his chant seems to confirm his worry.
Plume frowns. "Such a loss," he chants mournfully. Plume looks to he sky for a moment, then walks away.
"Thank you <first>!" His tone seems hopeful. "May the Embers light your way."
You find the <npc> adrift. They send a hail: "Please provide assistance. We were caught in the crossfire and our cloak stopped working!"

The crew of the <npc> is grateful for your assistance. In addition to a small payment of <payment>, they share what they've learned on their expedition. children.key: You find Taely pacing at the spaceport. She starts frantically signing when she notices you. "Captain <first>! A search and rescue team took a Peregrine named <npc> out into Korath space to locate one of Plume's missing research teams and didn't return on schedule. We fear the worst has happened to them. Would you be willing to search for them?"

Taely frowns. "I refuse to believe that," she signs. Taely then starts to walk away. She pauses, turning slightly and raising her arms as if to sign something. But instead, she lowers her hands in resignation and leaves.
"Thank you <first>!" The tone of her gestures seems hopeful. "May the Embers light your way."
You find the <npc> adrift. There are no responses to your hails. Board the ship to confirm the status of the crew."

The ship has been gutted. Black slime covers the internal walls and the leathery remains of Blight Shadow eggs are littered about. The only signs of the crew who were once aboard are some unidentifiable shriveled lumps in tattered Remnant clothing drenched with globs of the omnipresent black slime. There is no salvaging this ship. To remain here would doom yourself to sharing their fate. Return to <destination> and tell Taely what happened to the <npc>.

You share the bad news with Taely. She signs, "I'm sure the <npc> fought hard for its crew." Seemingly in mourning for the ship as well as the people who piloted it, she still thanks you for confirming their fate and arranges for <payment> to be deposited into your account.

Stain me hull green with their blood as you have! Return by <date>. Is more fun than staying on ringworld, no?" The Quarg in this region of space might not follow the details of human political affairs and are probably unaware of the Free Worlds...
A familiar Quarg yells out to you. "Human who hunts Blight Shadows! Is good to see again! You join me on hunt, yes? We be back by <date>." Quaelar-En seems eager to go on another hunting trip.

children.key: After finishing your business here, you notice an open doorway leading into restricted areas of the facility. You may not get another chance to see what lies beyond once the station is fully operational.
You walk through the doorway into empty hallways and dark corridors. No security guards are here to stop you. After a while, you get lost.
Your voice echoes through the empty passages. The silence that replies is filled with an eerie sense of loneliness.
You stumble down a dark corridor, hoping it will lead the way back to your ship when you suddenly hear a scream! That wasn't an echo...
You rush in the direction you think the scream originated. This leads you to a scattered pile of tools sitting in front of a sealed emergency blast door. Black slime oozes around the door's seams...
You strain against the door to no avail. Some of the black slime smears you...
(Try using the tools scattered on the floor.)

Looking through what's available, you find a laser cutter and begin cutting through the blast door. After several long minutes, you manage to poke a small hole into the door. The sound of air rushing into the hole can only mean one thing: The other side of the door is exposed to the external void of space! With some effort, you manage to weld the hole shut.
You knock on the door. There is no reaction.
You begin running away from the slime splattered door. After what seems like hours, you make it back to the docking bay where the <ship> sits undisturbed.

Your attempt to contact station management is successful. They inform you that a hull breach has occurred on another section of the station and they are working to contain it. There is nothing more for you to do.

missions.name: Midnight Docking Bay 13 Investigation
missions.description: Investigate the Power Generator attached to <stopovers>. Report your findings to <origin> to collect payment. (<payment>)

values: Investigate the Power Generator attached to <stopovers>. Report your findings to <origin> to collect payment. (<payment>)

children.key: Some time after landing, one of the station managers approaches you. "Captain <last>? Would you be able to take on a job only courageous captains like yourself can handle?"
"Quite a lot, actually. How does <payment> sound?"

"If you recall, Docking Bay 13 is currently not in use. The power to that section of the station is out. But our engineers have been unable to figure out why. We would like you to head over there and check things out."
"I'm a starship captain, not an engineer."
"Why doesn't your staff just go there?"

He hesitates before answering. "Well, you see, there are rumors that someone died during the construction of the station. And now people are afraid that a ghost is haunting that section. We don't actually expect you to fix the problem. Just verify that it's safe."
"Excellent! The internal security doors to that area are sealed, so you'll have to access it from outside."
(If you're having trouble finding it, open your map and double click on Docking Bay 13 on the Port data tab.)

You exit your ship with a flashlight and a thermal imager. The docking bay is eerily quiet. The area is dark, though there are occasional flashes of light from random lamps randomly flaring up before rapidly dimming. A doorway leads deeper into the station.
(Shine a flashlight around the docking bay.)

You move past the door and find a cargo bay. Several large crates occupy the room. It's too dark to clearly see the other side of the chamber. Nearby, a cooling duct blows a steady gust of air that sends a chill up your spine.
(Proceed to the far side of the cargo bay.)

As you approach the opposite wall, you find a dooway that's been ripped apart. Twisted sheets of metal that once separated this room from the area beynd lie mangled on the floor nearby. Through the doorway, you spot the generator that provides power to this section of the station. Several objects, obscured by the darkness, are clumped around it.

You walk towards the generator. It appears to be working. However the objects arranged around it are Blight Shadow eggs. Several tendrils growing out of the leathery membranes surrounding the eggs are attached to the generator, probably diverting power away from the station.

You draw your weapon and aim at the nearest egg. But before you can pull the trigger, you are suddenly surrounded by absolute darkness! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light suddenly fills your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. The leathery membranes on the eggs shift slightly in response, as if in anticipation for their occupants first meal...

You pause and quietly listen to your surroundings. The air shifts slightly and you are suddenly enveloped by absolute darkness! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light suddenly fills your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. It may be a while before anyone finds your corpse...

You sweep the docking area with your flashlight. You notice a patch of darkness above that your light can't seem to penetrate. Before you can fathom how far away the ceiling must be, the darkness suddenly drops towards you! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light suddenly fills your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. The flashlight lies a few feet away, its batteries as dead as you are.

Scanning the room with the thermal imager, you notice a blob of intense cold near the ceiling. Suddenly you are surrounded by absolute darkness! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light suddenly fills your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. Your corpse is covered in a thin layer of frost that quickly melts away. The thermal imager lies nearby, its batteries as dead as you are.

You shine your flashlight at the crates, causing a chaotic array of shadows to dance against the wall. You notice the crates closest to you contains food that expired months ago, an indicator of how long this area of the station has been abandoned. Before you can ponder this for too long, one of the shadows suddenly envelops you with absolute darkness! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light suddenly fills your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. The flashlight lies a few feet away, its batteries as dead as you are.
You approach the cooling duct. The air current is steady, unlike the lights. A small trickle of some sort of dark liquid is leaking out.

You take a closer look at the cooling duct. The dark liquid is black and viscuous. Something lashes out from inside the darkness of the dark duct and pulls you in! It happens so fast you don't even have time to scream before whatever it is kills you...
You scan the cargo bay with the thermal imager. A large mass of intense cold sits behind a group of crates on the other side of the room. It starts moving towards you...
You head towards the cold mass. As you close the distance, it vanishes from your thermal imager...

You shine your light at the strange objects and see that they are a cluster of Blight Shadow eggs. Several tendrils growing out of the leathery membranes surrounding the eggs are attached to the generator, probably diverting power away from the station.
You scan the area with your thermal imager. Whatever those objects are, they're leeching heat away from the generator...

You approach one of the eggs and reach out to it. Suddenly you are surrounded by absolute darkness! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light flashes to fill your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. The leathery membranes on the eggs shift slightly in response, as if in anticipation for their occupants first meal...

You turn to run and are suddenly enveloped by absolute darkness! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light suddenly fills your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. The flashlight lies a few feet away, its batteries as dead as you are.

You head back towards the docking bay. As you pass through the door, something knocks over a stack of crates in the cargo bay. A patch of darkness, blacker and more indistinct than the other shadows in the room, writhes among the scattered crates.

You head towards the scattered crates. Whatever caused the ruckus is nowhere to be seen. Suddenly you are surrounded by absolute darkness! You feel cold as a blindingly bright red light flashes to fill your vision. The darkness pulls away, dropping your desiccated husk onto the floor. Your corpse lies motionless, the room becoming still again.
You board the <ship> and launch, leaving the ominous shadows of Docking Bay 13 behind. The familiar stars of the Endless Sky are a welcome sight.
You are hailed by Titania Station. "Well Captain <first>, what did you find?"
"Everyone needs to get out of there."

The manager shouts, "That's not what I wanted to hear! Look, I'm sure whatever it is can't be that bad. Just take your payment and stay quiet about it. I'm not evacuating Titania just because some people think Docking Bay 13 is haunted." The manager transfers <payment> to your account and closes communications.

values: The Blight Shadows have reached The Twilight. Could they be following you?
This is where you fought the Alpha ship 'Giftbringer'. It might be a good idea to check the planet below for any renewed Alpha activity.

children.key: You spend a few hours scanning the planet for signs of Alpha activity. Fortunately, there are none. It would be a shame if some outside force threatened this primordial paradise. You take a moment to enjoy the scenery of exotic wildlife before returning to orbit.

You notice another fleet in the system. Apparently not all of the Kor Sestor were deactivated. But these look different from the models normally seen amongst their fleets. Perhaps it would be worth your while to board the big one and have a closer look.

Without a jump drive, it must have taken centuries for this ship to get here from Sestor space. The ship is loaded with equipment for construction. A colony ship? If this ship had established a base of operations on the planet below, the Sestor could rise again. The question is, how many other ships like this are out there?

values: The Kor Sestor sent expeditionary fleets beyond their space centuries ago. Without the limitations of old age, starvation, or anything else that would inhibit a normal crew, it is only a matter of time before these fleets eventually reach some place where they can establish a colony and begin a revival of the Kor Sestor automata.

children.key: You find a large cave entrance with some Sestor wreckage strewn about the entrance. It is large enough for the <ship> to fly in...

You take the <ship> in. This appears to be a former Sestor base. There are wrecked ships scattered about. Perhaps they went haywire when the Exiles shut down the central computers that controlled them. They don't appear to have been picked through by the Scrappers. But after a moment, you notice they broken hull of a Rano'erek lying among the wreckage. What will you do?

Taking the <ship> in closer, you note the scorch marks on the hull of the wrecked Rano'erek resembles damage done by Thermal Repeaters. Suddenly, a jumble of Sestor wreckage shifts and a ship rises from underneath! Then several more ships rise up, shaking off the detritus of wrecked Sestor ships that concealed them. These appear to be the same types of ships that were in the Sestor expeditionary fleet! They target your ship menacingly...
You turn the <ship> around and flee. The ancient Sestor ships pursue you out of the cave and into space!
The wreckage at the entrance seems like a bad omen warning you to stay away. You ignore the cave entrance and find a different place to land.
The wrecked Rano'erek must have been destroyed by something and you've decided not to risk waiting for whatever that is to return. You turn the <ship> around and fly out.

You fire on the hostile ships and they fire back. Several explode and the roof of the cave collapses, burying the <ship> under several tons of rock! The power goes out, plunging everything into darkness. Blind and buried alive, it is only a matter of time before you run out of oxygen...

values: These ships don't appear to be accompanied by a Grakerat 572. Perhaps they've gone rogue.
The larger ships in the rogue ancient Sestor fleet were outfitted with different weapons than the ones carried when accompanying a Grakerat 572...

children.key: You stumble upon a tragic scene. An old Kor Efret World-Ship named the <npc> is surrounded by blight shadows. The disabled ship hails you, and though you don't speak their language, it's obviously a distress call.

values: Damage to the Lekfarosk is severe and it will be a miracle if you can safely escort it back to <destination>.

children.key: The Kor Efret are grateful to you for saving them from certain death. They seem to want to give you a tour of their ship. It's an old antique, one of their genuine World-Ships. As the tour progresses, it becomes apparent that they are offering the ship to you as a gesture of thanks. While this seems like a generous reward, you can't help but notice that damage to the ship's key systems hasn't been repaired...
You notice a new type of ship under construction in the shipyard. While none are available for sale yet, the ship looks somewhat familiar...
A new warship is available for sale in the shipyard. A fleet of the new ships is on display.

missions.name: Scrapyard: Efret Salvage License 1
missions.description: Ask Rek to help you convince the Kor Efret to sell you weapons and other outfits installed on their ships.

values: Ask Rek to help you convince the Kor Efret to sell you weapons and other outfits installed on their ships.

children.key: With all the new ships being sold, you wonder if it's possible to buy the weapons and other outfits installed on them separately. Maybe Rek can help translate your request.

missions.name: Scrapyard: Efret Salvage License 2
missions.description: Ask Rek to help you convince the Kor Efret to sell you weapons and other outfits installed on their ships.

values: Ask Rek to help you convince the Kor Efret to sell you weapons and other outfits installed on their ships.

children.key: When you ask to meet Rek, you are told that she as returned to Setar Fort.

You find Rek giving a presentation at a meeting of some sort. It appears to be about the colony at Sabira Eseskrai, though you can't figure out the details. After waiting for her to finish, you approach her. "These shadow creature attacks have caused some colonists to have second thoughts about settling on planets farther than the Quarg ring. I can't blame them. The ship I was on was also attacked. It was an unnerving experience. The worst part wasn't the attack itself. It was being stranded in space on a derelict with no power and not knowing how long it would take for someone to rescue us... or if we'd even be rescued."
"It would help me fight the shadows if I were able to buy weapons from the Kor Efret."

"You have a valid point. Let's visit the outfitter and see if we can arrange something." After exchanging the customary greeting, Rek talks with the outfitter for a bit. The outfitter grabs something from the back of the shop and hands it to you. Rek translates, "Simply present this to any Kor Efret outfitter and they'll give you access to their stock of salvaged outfits."
Thanks to the local factories, the outfitter on Laki Nemparu is a bit more advanced than the other Kor Efret outfitters. Perhaps you can convince them to start manufacturing Korath Tormentors.
(Show the Korath Tormentor to the outfitter.)
The outfitter studies your Tormentor. It seems they want to buy it for 612,000 credits. Will you sell it?
(Sell the Korath Tormentor to the outfitter.)

The outfitter gladly pays you 612,000 credits and some technicians cart the weapon away. Hopefully they'll use it as a prototype to manufacture more, but with the language barrier, you can't be certain what their plans for it are.
You notice a demonstration of the Tormentor taking place at the outfitter. It appears they are available for purchase.

You notice something wrong when you enter Chimitarp: There isn't any fighting. The Mereti are standing by, as if waiting for orders. Suddenly, a Korath Devourer hails you! You raise an eyebrow when you learn the ship's name: Damnation. You're fairly certain that isn't a Korath name.
"Greetings <ship>. Captain <last>, was it? I've heard about you. While the Scrappers are content to collect scraps, I've taken possession of a far greater prize. Welcome to hell.
Without bothering to answer, the Damnation jumps out of the system as the Mereti activate and surround you...

children.key: Unfortunately, the battle outside did not go unnoticed. The Damnation flees the station just as you finish landing! You need to board that ship and learn how they're controlling the Mereti.

values: The Blight Shadows have made it this far without the Kor Mereti to hold them back. The sooner you bring the Mereti back to normal, the better.
The Blight Shadows have made it this far without the Kor Mereti to hold them back. The sooner you bring the Mereti back to normal, the better.
Looks like the Damnation ran into a little trouble. Board the ship and learn how they're controlling the Mereti!

children.key: This is an Alpha ship crewed by enslaved humans and Korath. Amid the chaos of the boarding battle, you find a solitary Alpha too preoccupied with a device that resembles a clump of Reasoning Nodes to notice you.

He sighs in resignation. "They're too difficult to control. At most, I can handle ten thousand. Maybe twenty. Do you have any idea what it's like performing high level brain surgery on twenty thousand Kor Mereti at once?" He turns towards you. "No, of course not. How could you? A normal human couldn't manage it."
The Alpha springs into action! You fire off several shots, but he's fast! He manages to dodge them all and is rapidly closing the distance between you...
He grabs you by the neck and slams you onto the floor like a ragdoll. As you lose consciousness, you regret not shooting him in the back...

But you are the demon captain of atrocity. The power of Midnight's Lost Orphan flows through you and the Alpha finds himself writhing on the floor in agony as you enjoy a perverse pleasure in psychopathically rearranging his internal organs.

Normally, you'd be no match for an Alpha in this situation. Fortunately, you've got something to even the odds. You draw the Quantum Key Blade and Quantum Shift just as the Alpha tries to disarm you. His hands pass through the blade, unable to grab it. As he looks at you in shock, you plunge the blade into his chest and deactivate Quantum Shifting. The Alpha slumps to the floor, defeated.
But T.H.O.R. swoops in and nails him with the arm mounted pile driver! Even a genetically enhanced human is no match for the Tactical Heavy Offensive Robot.
You shoot the Alpha in the back and he dies without a word. Underhanded, but this is an Alpha. Trying to take him head on would be suicide without something extraordinary to even the odds.
You can figure out what to do with this strange assembly of Reasoning Nodes later. There's still a battle to fight!

You find the remains of a dead Korath boarding party. All that remains of their corpses are withered husks. One of their rifles is still intact. A few empty Blight Shadow eggs are scattered across the floor of a nearby chamber...

You find a room splattered with black slime. It covers the floor, the walls, and some even drips from the ceiling. Fragments of black leathery egg shells are scattered about. But whoever left this mess is long gone. You turn to leave but slip on a puddle of slime and wind up on the floor, splattered with the disgusting goo. It might be a good idea to decontaminate your environmental suit later...
Some of the equipment here is still active. After studying it for a while, you conclude that the ship's computer is trying to send out a distress signal.
Some of the equipment here is still active. After studying it for a while, you conclude that the ship's computer is trying to send out a distress signal.
You find a gaping hole where a section of the hull was blasted off. While looking out into the darkness, you are almost certain that you saw something move out there...

Suddenly the derelict lurches violently. That was an impact! You rush back to your ship to find the warning alarms going off. A large fleet of scrappers just made a strafing run. Better fight them off if you don't want your own ship to become a Scrapyard derelict!

If it were simply [raids, pillaging] from the exiles, the Mereti would not be referring to them as 'shadows [lurking, hiding] in the darkness'. No, it must be something else."

children.key: You enter the system to find a strange scene playing out. An archon is helping a small fleet of Kor exiles kill off a swarm of some shadowy creatures.

"These Blight Shadows are an invasive species from outside our galaxy," the archon's telepathic voice fills your head. "Some of the exiles have offered to help eradicate them from their home region of the galaxy."
"Are you ending the exile of the Korath?"
"Kill as many shadows as you can. They are invaders and not welcome in our galaxy."

"These invaders simply traveled through the empty void between galaxies. While their bodies can absorb many different kinds of energies, they seem to thrive by feeding on the power generated by starships as well as the material that composes the ships themselves. The battlegrounds of the Kor automatons were a perfect nesting ground for these creatures. By happenstance or natural instinct, the Sestor's territory was where the shadows chose to embed themselves. For hundreds of years, the Sestor have been keeping them suppressed."
"But now that the Sestor are gone..."
"Yes. Now that the Sestor are gone, the Blight Shadows are feeding on the defenseless derelicts that were left behind and are growing in number."

"No. We are merely allowing scrappers, who have volunteered their assistance in eradicating this threat, to scavenge the leftover derelicts from the Mereti/Sestor war. In doing so, they are removing the food that the Blight Shadows thrive on."
"The archon and the Kor scrappers continue their battle with the shadows from beyond the galaxy."

values: Scrapyard: Meeting on Desi Seledrak: done

children.key: You've eliminated some of the derelicts, but more are out there waiting to be exploited by Scrappers and Blight Shadows.
A subsidurial is surrounded by blight shadows. You could intervene if you want to.

The subsidurial comes to a rest on the adjacent landing pad. It seems to have fallen asleep. Several Wanderers gawk at it in exasperation. As you disembark your ship, some look to you for an explanation. You tell them that it came here on its own. Hopefully you won't get blamed for any damage it does to the spaceport while you're here...

values: There's an old space station here. It might be worth checking out.

children.key: You notice a derelict scrapper ship docked at the station. Explore the ship?
The ship has a breathable atmosphere. Life support appears to be the only system still working. Everything else seems to have already been looted for spare parts.

Several control panels have been ripped out of their consoles, leaving exposed wires everywhere. You might be able to get the internal sensors working if you're willing to roll up your sleeves and get your hands dirty.
(Search a different part of the ship.)
While trying to get the internal sensors working, an exposed power cable falls out of the ceiling and electrocutes you!

You find yourself in the cargo bay surrounded by several pieces of equipment in various states of deconstruction. The only intact items are a few crates of control transceivers and reasoning nodes. As you close a crate, you hear a noise in the distance. It sounds like something scampering away.
The main power systems are offline. Try to fix them?
(Search a different part of the ship.)
When you restore the power systems, a nearby plasma conduit bursts open, smothering you in molten plasma!
The engine room door seems to be stuck. Force it open?
(Search a different part of the ship.)

You force the engine room doors open only to find that the room has been depressurized. Parts of the hull have been melted away, leaving the room exposed to the vacuum outside. The sudden change in pressure shoots you out of the ship into the vast empty void.
You are about to leave when you hear a noise in the distance. It sounds like something scampering away.

You find the armory. Most of the weapon racks are empty while a few repeater rifles are scattered about the floor. But what really draws your attention is the freshly cut hole in the wall. The edges of the hole are still glowing red hot. A repeater rifle couldn't have made this.

You carefully crawl through the hole. This seems to be some sort of maintenance tunnel. Suddenly a beam of energy punches through the tunnel ahead of you! It vanishes and another one appears behind you. Someone is shooting through the walls at you, but at least they're shooting blind! After several twists and turns, you manage to find another hole melted through the wall without having any holes melted through yourself. Going through it, you emerge at one of the ship's fighter bays. A heavily modified Korath Chaser is powering up its engines for take off!

You've decided not to let whoever that is escape. After a frenzied rush through unfamiliar hallways, you make it back to your ship in time to see the fighter bay doors on the other ship open. Release the docking clamps!

Whatever melted that hole through the wall isn't something you want to mess with. You gather up the rifles from the floor and the crate of equipment from the cargo bay. It's a small haul, but it's better than nothing.

That was an odd looking ship. Too bad you won't be able to get a closer look at it. You head back to the armory and gather up the rifles from the floor. You also remember to hit up the cargo bay for the crates of equipment you found earlier. It's a small haul, but it's better than nothing.

values: This modified chaser was occupied by a single Korath warrior armed with a strange rifle. You should probably look it over once you get to an outfitter.
